_comment: Function entries the CN/JP build calls but that the address map cannot place.
Each was found at run time: the build reports an indirect branch into the
address with the call context (ra, sp, gp, registers), and 'why' records what
that context proved.  They are added as function entries in the target so the
recompiler emits them, because a call through a function pointer appears in no
call instruction and so cannot be recovered from the call graph either.
They exist because the two builds disagree about function boundaries in the
text/font region (around 0x003601xx) badly enough that several reference
functions map onto one target address.  Those functions are a family of
near-identical small helpers, so matching their code cannot separate them; the
addresses have to be stated, not derived.
Add an entry here when a build reports:
==== indirect branch to XXXXXXXX, which no recompiled function claims ====
and the address is a plausible function entry (a frame prologue) in the target.
The warning names the register holding the target and the return address, which
together identify the caller in the reference binary.
target  : the address in the target (CN/JP) build that must become a function
ref     : a reference (US) function whose code matches it, so the recompiler can
name it and the port can carry the entry across
why     : the evidence, kept so a later reader does not have to re-derive it

0x00361260.why: reported as an indirect branch 285 times; the caller is target 0035F748 (reference 0035F408), which does 'lw r2, gp+0xDAC8' then 'jalr r2', so the address comes from a data pointer and is in no call instruction. The reference twin is a frame prologue with the same ten-instruction opening; the map instead places it on 003611A4.

0x0028B870.why: reported as an indirect branch target with the same call context as 00361260. Sits inside the mapped function 0028B800, whose reference counterpart has different bounds; the target's own entry is missing from the table.

0x0028B890.why: same as 0028B870: a second entry inside mapped function 0028B800 that the table does not have.
